summary.en: Israel has intensified cross-border operations, striking a Hezbollah weapons shipment in Lebanon's eastern Beqaa Valley and demolishing a Hezbollah tunnel in southern Lebanon, while an Israeli drone was filmed flying low over homes in southern Lebanon. US envoy Waltz visited Beirut to demand Hezbollah disarmament, and Israel claimed to have kidnapped Iranian generals in a bid to locate Ron Arad. The conflict has caused 4,335 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Israel har økt grenseoverskridende operasjoner, og har slått et Hezbollah-våpenforsendelse i Libanons østlige Bekaa-dal og revet ned en Hezbollah-tunnel i sørlige Libanon, mens en israelsk drone ble filmet i lav høyde over hus i sørlige Libanon. USAs representant Waltz besøkte Beirut for å kreve at Hezbollah avlegger våpnene, og Israel hevdet at de har kidnappet iranske generaler i et forsøk på å lokalisere Ron Arad. Konflikten har forårsaket 4 335 dødsfall i kamper i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Hezbollah–Israel conflict (2023–present)
background.extract: An ongoing conflict between the Lebanese militant group Hezbollah and Israel began on 8 October 2023, when Hezbollah launched rockets and artillery at Israeli positions following Hamas's October 7 attacks on Israel. The conflict escalated into a prolonged exchange of bombardments, leading to extensive displacement in Israel and Lebanon. The conflict is part of the broader Middle Eastern crisis that began with Hamas's attack, with the short Israeli invasion of Lebanon in 2024 marking the largest escalation of the Hezbollah–Israel conflict since the 2006 Lebanon War. In Arabic, the conflict (2023–2024) is referred to as the "Support War" or the "Gaza Support War."
